root_cause.text: In openvswitch's push_nsh action validation, flow_netlink.c blindly double-unwrapped nested netlink attributes with nla_data() without validating the intermediate attribute, so a malformed middle OVS_KEY_ATTR_NSH container could have an invalid type/length and trigger out-of-bounds access.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states “nothing checks if the attribute in the middle is OK,” “We don't even check that this attribute is the OVS_KEY_ATTR_NSH,” and that the code “just do[es] a double unwrap with a pair of nla_data() calls”; the patch fixes this by changing validate_push_nsh() to validate the middle nlattr with nla_ok(), size equality via nla_total_size(nla_len(nsh_key)) != nla_len(a), and nla_type(nsh_key) != OVS_KEY_ATTR_NSH before calling nsh_key_put_from_nlattr().

agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message states “nothing checks if the attribute in the middle is OK,” “We don't even check that this attribute is the OVS_KEY_ATTR_NSH,” and that the code “just do[es] a double unwrap with a pair of nla_data() calls”; the patch fixes this by changing validate_push_nsh() to validate the middle nlattr with nla_ok(), size equality via nla_total_size(nla_len(nsh_key)) != nla_len(a), and nla_type(nsh_key) != OVS_KEY_ATTR_NSH before calling nsh_key_put_from_nlattr().

intent_record.intent_summary: Add strict validation that push-NSH netlink data contains exactly one OVS_KEY_ATTR_NSH nested attribute before parsing it.
intent_record.what: The function parameter in validate_push_nsh() was renamed from attr to a, a new local nlattr pointer nsh_key was initialized with nla_data(a), and a validation block was added to require that the payload contains exactly one nested attribute and that its type is OVS_KEY_ATTR_NSH using nla_ok(), nla_total_size(nla_len(nsh_key)) == nla_len(a), and nla_type(). The call to nsh_key_put_from_nlattr() was updated to pass nsh_key instead of the outer attribute.
intent_record.how: At runtime, validate_push_nsh() now verifies that the provided netlink attribute contains one valid nested NSH attribute and rejects malformed, extra, or wrong-typed payloads before attempting to parse them. This prevents parsing the outer container as the NSH key and avoids accepting invalid push NSH action data.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix NSH push action validation by passing the netlink attribute itself to validate_push_nsh() instead of its payload data pointer.
intent_record.what: The call to validate_push_nsh() was changed to pass the nlattr pointer variable a directly instead of passing nla_data(a).
intent_record.how: At runtime, validate_push_nsh() now receives the full netlink attribute object rather than only its payload pointer, allowing it to interpret or validate the NSH push action using the expected input type and preventing incorrect validation behavior caused by passing the wrong argument.

grouping_result.intent: Add strict validation that push-NSH netlink data contains exactly one OVS_KEY_ATTR_NSH nested attribute before parsing it.
Fix NSH push action validation by passing the netlink attribute itself to validate_push_nsh() instead of its payload data pointer.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by validating that the push-NSH netlink payload contains exactly one properly nested OVS_KEY_ATTR_NSH attribute before unwrapping/parsing it, preventing the blind double-nla_data() handling of malformed intermediate attributes.

The change directly addresses the root cause in push_nsh validation: instead of passing a raw payload pointer from nla_data() and effectively double-unwrapping nested attributes, it passes the netlink attribute itself so the intermediate NSH container can be properly validated before accessing nested data.

candidates.rationale: This passes only the payload pointer of the outer netlink attribute into validate_push_nsh(), causing the validator to treat untrusted inner bytes as a struct nlattr and blindly unwrap nested attributes without first validating the intermediate container.

This directly invokes NSH parsing on the provided attr as if it were a valid nlattr container; when called with nla_data(a) instead of a validated nlattr, it can parse a malformed intermediate OVS_KEY_ATTR_NSH attribute and reach out-of-bounds memory.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the primary vulnerable call site. It passes only the payload pointer of the outer netlink attribute via nla_data(a) into validate_push_nsh(), causing the callee to interpret unvalidated inner bytes as a struct nlattr and perform a second unwrap without validating the intermediate OVS_KEY_ATTR_NSH container.

This validation routine blindly forwards attr to the NSH parser without first ensuring the push-NSH netlink data is exactly one valid OVS_KEY_ATTR_NSH nested attribute. When reached from the bad caller that passed nla_data(a), this contributes directly to parsing a malformed intermediate attribute and enables out-of-bounds access.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it directly shows the relevant NSH validation paths. The vulnerable area described in the root cause is validation of nested NSH attributes, especially for set(nsh(...)). In this commit, support for setting NSH fields has been removed from validate_set(): the entire `case OVS_KEY_ATTR_NSH:` block was deleted from `validate_set`, including the call `validate_nsh(nla_data(a), masked, false, log)`. That means the problematic set(nsh(...)) validation path is no longer present in this version. The helper was also narrowed from `validate_nsh(const struct nlattr *attr, bool is_mask, bool is_push_nsh, bool log)` to `validate_push_nsh(const struct nlattr *attr, bool log)`, and now always calls `nsh_key_put_from_nlattr(attr, &match, false, true, log)`, i.e. only for push_nsh validation. Since the bug root cause specifically concerns malformed nested attributes during set(nsh(...)) / double-unwrapping validation, and that set path is absent here, the vulnerable construct is not present in this commit version. Therefore `has_bug=false` and `is_fixed=true`.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it directly shows the relevant validation path for NSH actions. The root cause concerns validation of nested NSH netlink attributes, especially in set(nsh(...)) handling. In this commit, support for `OVS_KEY_ATTR_NSH` inside `validate_set()` is removed entirely: the whole case block `case OVS_KEY_ATTR_NSH: ... if (!validate_nsh(nla_data(a), masked, false, log)) return -EINVAL;` is deleted. That means the vulnerable set(nsh(...)) validation path is no longer present in this version. The replacement also narrows validation to push_nsh only: `static bool validate_push_nsh(const struct nlattr *attr, bool log)` now always calls `nsh_key_put_from_nlattr(attr, &match, false, true, log)`, removing the previous generic `validate_nsh(..., is_mask, is_push_nsh, ...)` interface that was used for both push_nsh and set(nsh(...)) cases. The comment added above `nsh_hdr_from_nlattr()` explicitly says it is for `OVS_ACTION_ATTR_PUSH_NSH` and assumes prior validation with `validate_push_nsh()`. Therefore, the vulnerable construct described in the root cause—blind double-unwrapping during set(nsh(...)) action validation—is absent here, and the fix is present by removing never-working support for setting NSH fields.
